skill.name: okx-dapp-discovery
skill.description: Routes supported DeFi DApp requests to the matching OKX plugin. It detects protocol names, native tokens, comparisons, and English or Chinese intent before requesting installation consent.
skill.summary: Discover supported DeFi DApps, select the correct OKX plugin, and continue the original request after approval.
skill.author: okx

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, DeFi terminology, or protective consent guidance rather than dangerous behavior. Confirmed behavior includes `npx` execution, global plugin installation, and a user-approved GitHub catalog request. The mutable plugin source creates a medium supply-chain risk despite explicit consent and fetched-content safeguards.

remediation.issue: The skills CLI and plugin registry content are not pinned to immutable versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI version and plugin source commit, then verify a published digest or signature before global installation and loading.

remediation.issue: The installed-status check can execute or download an `npx` package before installation consent.
remediation.suggestion: Use a locally verified CLI binary, or request approval before any `npx` invocation that may fetch and execute package code.

content.user_title: Discover and Route OKX DApp Plugins
content.value_statement: Choosing the correct DeFi plugin can be difficult across protocols and intent types. This skill identifies supported DApps, requests installation consent, and resumes the original task.
actual_capabilities: Maps supported DApp names and native tokens to 20 plugin entries.
Recognizes routing intent in English and Chinese prompts.
Distinguishes direct actions, comparisons, informational requests, and generic DeFi requests.
Checks installed plugins and requests confirmation before a missing plugin is installed.
Shows supported alternatives and offers a consented catalog lookup for unknown DApps.
Reapplies the original request after loading the selected plugin.
limitations: It routes requests but does not sign or broadcast blockchain transactions.
It supports only the protocols and variants listed in its resolver table.
Protocol information and transaction behavior depend on the installed plugin.
Catalog lookup and plugin installation require network access and external command execution.

use_cases.title: Find a Supported DApp
use_cases.description: Review the available lending, trading, staking, prediction, and liquidity protocols before choosing one.

use_cases.title: Route a Protocol Action
use_cases.description: Map a named protocol action or native token request to the correct plugin and request installation approval.
use_cases.target_user: Wallet users preparing a DeFi task

use_cases.title: Resolve Multilingual Intent
use_cases.description: Interpret English or Chinese DApp requests while preserving protocol-specific routing and clarification rules.
use_cases.target_user: Support teams handling multilingual Web3 requests

prompt_templates.title: List Supported DApps
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the supported DApps by category and explain which option fits my goal: [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Route a Direct Action
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to [action] [amount and token] on [DApp]. Select the correct plugin and ask before installing it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Supported Protocols
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [DApp A] and [DApp B] for [goal]. Do not install anything until I choose.

prompt_templates.title: Handle an Unknown DApp
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [DApp] is supported. Show close alternatives and offer a catalog lookup without installing anything automatically.

output_examples.input: What DApps can I use for lending?
output_examples.output: Supported lending options include Aave V3, Compound V3, Kamino Lend, and Morpho V1 Optimizer. Which protocol matches your goal?
This request maps to the Aave V3 plugin. I will ask for installation approval before continuing if the plugin is missing.
I can discuss their tradeoffs or set up either plugin. No plugin will be installed until you choose.

best_practices: Name the DApp, action, token, and amount when requesting protocol routing.
Review every plugin installation prompt and transaction approval separately.
Use comparison prompts before installation when multiple protocols may fit.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private keys, seed phrases, API keys, passwords, or session tokens.
Do not treat plugin installation as approval for a blockchain transaction.
Do not expect unsupported protocol variants to map to the closest plugin automatically.

faq.question: Does this skill execute transactions?
faq.answer: No. It routes requests and loads plugins. Wallet approval is still required for every blockchain write.

faq.question: Does it install plugins automatically?
faq.answer: No. A missing plugin requires explicit confirmation before installation.

faq.question: Which protocols are supported?
faq.answer: The resolver covers 20 entries across prediction markets, lending, perpetuals, swaps, staking, yield trading, and meme launchpads.

faq.question: Can it understand Chinese requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The included glossary defines Chinese aliases, actions, native-token phrases, and routing examples.

faq.question: What happens when a DApp is unsupported?
faq.answer: It shows supported alternatives and can offer a user-approved, read-only catalog lookup.

faq.question: Can it compare protocols without installing plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. Comparison requests can remain informational until you choose a protocol and approve installation.
